scenario: The school assistant should always respond in simple English and never use jargon — this standard applies to every reply it ever gives.
explanation: Always-on guidance across all interactions = Rule. It is passive direction, not an action.

scenario: When a student asks for help writing an essay, the assistant follows a specific 5-step workflow: brainstorm → outline → draft → peer-review checklist → final polish.
explanation: A repeatable multi-step procedure for a specific task = Skill. It is on-demand expertise.

scenario: The assistant can search lecture notes, retrieve past exam questions, and send a calendar invite.
explanation: Callable actions on files and systems during a task = Tools. MCP from Week 5 is one way to standardise tool access.

scenario: Before the assistant saves any file, a script runs automatically to check the format and block files over 10MB.
explanation: Event-triggered automation at a lifecycle moment (before save) = Hook. Reactive, not conversational.

scenario: The class project installs a documentation browser so the agent can look up API references while helping students code.
explanation: An installable packaged capability added to the environment = Plugin.

scenario: For a large research assignment, one agent finds sources, another drafts the bibliography, and the lead agent combines both outputs.
explanation: Focused parallel workers with separate context and clear handoffs = Subagents.

scenario: The assistant must always cite the document it pulled information from — no citation means no answer.
explanation: Persistent standard applied to every answer = Rule.

scenario: When the assistant finishes a tutoring session, a script logs how long the session lasted and saves the summary to the student's profile.
explanation: Post-event automated action at a lifecycle moment = Hook.

scenario: A team shares a ready-made integration that adds calendar scheduling and email drafting to any school AI assistant.
explanation: A shareable packaged capability bundle = Plugin.

scenario: Each time a student asks for exam practice, the assistant follows a set procedure: pick past questions → time the student → mark answers → suggest weak areas.
explanation: A repeatable domain procedure triggered on demand = Skill.

scenario: For a website project, one subagent writes the HTML, another writes the CSS, and a third writes the JavaScript. The lead agent reviews and combines.
explanation: Work split across specialised parallel agents with clear handoffs = Subagents.

scenario: The assistant can read class schedules, update a shared to-do list, and send notifications to the teacher.
explanation: Callable actions on data and systems = Tools.
